title: Effect of exenatide on heart rate and blood pressure in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized pilot study

citation.title: Effect of exenatide on heart rate and blood pressure in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized pilot study

printed_heading.text: ORIGINAL INVESTIGATION Open Access Effect of exenatide on heart rate and blood pressure in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized pilot study Anne Gill1 , Byron J Hoogwerf2 , Jude Burger1 , Simon Bruce3 , Leigh MacConell3 , Ping Yan3 , Daniel Braun1 , Joseph Giaconia1 , James Malone1*

what_it_measured.text: Our aim was to assess the effects of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist exenatide on heart rate (HR) and blood pressure (BP) in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

dose.text: Methods: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, subjects with T2DM on metformin and/or a thiazolidinedione were randomized to receive exenatide (5 μg for 4 weeks followed by 10 μg) or placebo BID for 12 weeks.
At Week 4, exenatide dose was escalated from 5 μg to 10 μg BID, which was continued for the remaining 8 weeks.

route.text: In this multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, subjects received subcutaneous placebo injections during a 1-week placebo lead-in before randomization to exenatide or placebo BID for 12 weeks.

endpoint.text: The primary measure was change from baseline in mean 24-hour HR.

reported_results.text: With exenatide, body weight decreased from baseline by -1.8 ± 0.4 kg (p < 0.0001; treatment difference -1.5 ± 0.6 kg, p < 0.05).

At 12 weeks, no significant change from baseline in 24-hour HR was observed with exenatide or placebo (LS mean ± SE, 2.1 ± 1.4 versus -0.7 ± 1.4 beats/minute, respectively; between treatments, p = 0.16).

Baseline values (exenatide and placebo) were (mean ± SE) 74.4 ± 2.1 and 74.5 ± 1.9 beats/minute for HR, 126.4 ± 3.2 and 119.9 ± 2.8 mm Hg for systolic BP (SBP), and 75.2 ± 2.1 and 70.5 ± 2.0 mm Hg for diastolic BP (DBP).
There was a -0.3 ± 0.2% reduction in hemoglobin A 1c for exenatide relative to placebo (p = 0.26).
Exenatide reduced mean body weight from baseline by -1.8 ± 0.4 kg (p < 0.0001) at Week 12, whereas placebo resulted in no significant change (-0.3 ± 0.4 kg, p = 0.52).
Of note, immediately after dose escalation, exenatide was associated with a small, transient increase in LS mean 24-hour HR change from baseline (3.4 ± 1.6 beats/minute, p < 0.05).
